name: bee

attributes.attribute: a rare symbol of wisdom in Celtic legend
said to drop down from heaven to the earth
carried by fishermen as an amulet of safety at sea
a saint tied to the craft of beekeeping
a Munster nun tied to the craft of beekeeping

sources: Killip, Margaret. The Folklore of the Isle of Man. London: B. T. Batsford, Ltd., 1975, 76.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
Bees rarely appear in Celtic legend. When they do come, they stand for wisdom. The bee was said to be a drop that fell from heaven.

On the Isle of Man, fishermen caught bees in the early spring. Each sailor carried a bee as an amulet of safety at sea. In Ireland the bee had no pre-Christian mark of religion. Some Irish saints still kept bees. The Welsh saint Domnoc and the Munster nun Gobnat were tied to the craft of keeping bees.

okr.objective: Describe the bee as a rare but symbolic insect in Celtic legend.
key_results: Bees appear as a symbol of wisdom in rare Celtic tales.
The bee was said to fall from heaven to the earth.
Isle of Man fishermen carried bees as amulets at sea.
Saint Domnoc and the nun Gobnat became linked to bees.
